1.0.8: Sync with your iPhone: scan a QR code in Settings with Fjord for iPhone, and your history, bookmarks and open tabs go both ways over your home Wi-Fi. Nothing goes through the internet.
Spaces: separate sets of tabs like Work and Personal, each with its own colour. The button at the start of the tabs switches between them.
Privacy report in Settings: what Fjord blocked each day this week, which companies tried to track you and on which sites. It stays on this computer.
24 new photos on the new tab.
Windows: no more stray “Fjord Private Browsing” shortcut in the Start menu.
1.0.7: Mac: Fjord.dmg opens a small window that shows you to drag Fjord into Applications.
Mac: Fjord starts with its own icon instead of Firefox's, and macOS no longer warns that Fjord tried to read another app's data.
1.0.6: Private YouTube player: videos play on their own, without recommendations or your YouTube history. Turn it on the first time you watch something, or in Privacy.
Randomised fingerprint: every site gets slightly different canvas, WebGL and audio readings, so sites can't use them to recognise you.
Hide parts of pages: right-click a cookie wall, sidebar or pop-up and choose “Hide this”. Shields can show it again.
Command bar: Ctrl+K (⌘K on a Mac) finds your tabs, bookmarks, history and Fjord's actions.
Link preview: Shift-click a link to open it over the page.
1.0.5: After an update, Fjord tells you what's new, like this.
Forget this site: one click in Shields deletes a site's cookies, saved data and history.
Reader view in Fjord's font and colours.
Linux on ARM computers, with its own download.
